themeHint: Think stars and stripes.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: American astronaut who took 'one small step' onto the Moon in 1969.
clues.fact: Neil Armstrong was a US Navy pilot before he became an astronaut.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Large reptile with a broad snout that lurks in Florida swamps.
clues.fact: The American alligator is the official state reptile of Florida.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: The largest US state, bought from Russia in 1867.
clues.fact: Alaska is the largest US state by area, more than twice the size of Texas.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Invention the Wright brothers first flew at Kitty Hawk in 1903.
clues.fact: The Wright brothers' first powered flight in 1903 lasted only about 12 seconds.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Dessert in the saying 'as American as...': a pastry crust filled with sliced orchard fruit.
clues.fact: Apple pie recipes were written down in England centuries before the United States existed.

clues.label: Award
clues.clue: Hollywood's top film prize, a golden statuette better known as the Oscar.
clues.fact: The first Academy Awards ceremony was held in 1929.

themeHint: Waves, salt water and ships.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Disney's red-haired mermaid who trades her voice for a pair of legs.
clues.fact: The Little Mermaid is based on a fairy tale by Danish author Hans Christian Andersen.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Huge seabird with the longest wingspan of any bird, gliding over oceans for days.
clues.fact: The wandering albatross has the largest wingspan of any living bird, over 3 metres.

clues.clue: Ocean whose waves roll onto Lagos beaches, and the beaches of Brazil on the other side.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Heavy hooked object dropped overboard to stop a ship drifting.
clues.fact: The earliest anchors were simply heavy stones tied to a rope.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Tiny, very salty fish often laid on top of pizzas.
clues.fact: Anchovies are small fish that swim in huge schools.

clues.label: Job
clues.clue: Top-ranking naval officer who commands a whole fleet.
clues.fact: Horatio Nelson was a British admiral famous for winning the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805.

themeHint: Tea, rain and red phone boxes.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: England football star who married a Spice Girl.
clues.fact: David Beckham played for Manchester United, Real Madrid and LA Galaxy, among others.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Stocky, wrinkly dog seen as a symbol of British toughness.
clues.fact: Bulldogs were originally bred in England for the cruel sport of bull-baiting.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Famous bell in the clock tower beside the Houses of Parliament in London.
clues.fact: Big Ben is officially the name of the great bell; the tower is called the Elizabeth Tower.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Red double-decker vehicle that carries passengers around London.
clues.fact: London's red double-decker buses are a world-famous symbol of the city.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Sausages with creamy potato and onion gravy, a classic British pub meal.
clues.fact: Sausages got the nickname 'bangers' because they can burst with a bang when fried.

clues.label: Music
clues.clue: Liverpool band of John, Paul, George and Ringo.
clues.fact: The Beatles are widely regarded as the best-selling music act of all time.

themeHint: Think of the Taj Mahal's home country.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Amitabh ___, Bollywood legend who has starred in hundreds of films.
clues.fact: Amitabh Bachchan has long hosted the Indian version of 'Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?'.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Striped big cat that is the country's national animal.
clues.fact: The Bengal tiger is the national animal of India.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Old name of Mumbai, the country's biggest city.
clues.fact: The city officially changed its name from Bombay to Mumbai in 1995.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Decorative dot worn on the forehead, between the eyebrows.
clues.fact: A bindi can be a simple red dot or a sparkly stick-on jewel.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Fragrant spiced rice dish layered with meat or vegetables.
clues.fact: The city of Hyderabad is famous for its own style of this rice dish.

clues.label: Film
clues.clue: Nickname of the Hindi-language film industry based in Mumbai.
clues.fact: India produces more films each year than any other country.

themeHint: The coldest season of the year.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Santa's surname; he does his busiest work on cold December nights.
clues.fact: The name Santa Claus comes from the Dutch Sinterklaas, based on Saint Nicholas.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: North American name for the reindeer, which survives freezing Arctic winters.
clues.fact: Caribou and reindeer are the same species.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Huge snowy country north of the USA with a maple leaf on its flag.
clues.fact: Canada has the longest coastline of any country in the world.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Warm outer garment you button up before going out into the snow.
clues.fact: Down coats are filled with the soft under-feathers of ducks or geese.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Hot chocolatey drink that warms you up on a frosty day.
clues.fact: Most of the world's cocoa beans are grown in West Africa, with Ivory Coast and Ghana the biggest producers.

clues.label: Sport
clues.clue: Ice sport where players sweep in front of a sliding granite stone.
clues.fact: Many curling stones are made from granite quarried on Ailsa Craig, an island off Scotland.

themeHint: Saloons, sheriffs and tumbleweeds.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Famous frontierswoman and sharpshooter, a friend of Wild Bill Hickok.
clues.fact: Calamity Jane's real name was Martha Jane Cannary.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Wild dog of the prairies, famous for howling at night.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Spicy stew of beef, beans and peppers, cooked by cattle drivers on the trail.
clues.fact: Chili con carne is the official state dish of Texas.

clues.label: Job
clues.clue: Ranch worker on horseback who herds cattle and wears a wide-brimmed hat.

themeHint: Kangaroos hop here.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: 'Crocodile' hero of a 1986 film, played by Paul Hogan.
clues.fact: Crocodile Dundee was one of the most successful Australian films ever made.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Wild yellow dog of the Outback.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Tropical capital city of the Northern Territory.
clues.fact: The city is named after the naturalist Charles Darwin.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Long wooden wind instrument played by Aboriginal people, with a deep droning sound.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Simple bush bread baked in the hot coals of a campfire.

clues.label: Slang
clues.clue: Aussie slang for a fool; also a glossy black bird with a forked tail.

themeHint: Think Berlin, beer halls and the autobahn.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Rudolf ___, German engineer whose surname is now on fuel pumps everywhere.
clues.fact: Rudolf Diesel was born in Paris to German parents.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Long, low 'sausage dog' bred to hunt badgers.

clues.label: Food

clues.fact: The doner kebab sandwich became hugely popular in Berlin thanks to Turkish immigrants.

clues.label: Language
clues.clue: What the locals call their own language.
clues.fact: German is the most widely spoken native language in the European Union.

themeHint: Crowns, thrones and palaces.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: British queen who reigned for 70 years until 2022.
clues.fact: Queen Elizabeth II was the longest-reigning British monarch in history.

clues.clue: Largest of the flightless tuxedo-wearing birds of Antarctica, named after a royal title.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: White fur with black tips used to trim royal robes and crowns.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Bergamot-flavoured black tea named after a British nobleman.

clues.label: Title
clues.clue: Female ruler of an empire.
clues.fact: Queen Victoria was also given the title Empress of India.

themeHint: Feathers, beaks and wings.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: 'The Eagle', the British ski jumper who charmed the 1988 Winter Olympics.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Tall Australian bird that cannot fly.

clues.clue: Florida wetland famous for its herons, egrets and alligators.

clues.clue: Quilt originally stuffed with the soft down of a northern sea duck.
clues.fact: Eider ducks line their nests with their own soft down, which is collected for bedding.

clues.clue: Laid by hens and eaten boiled, fried or scrambled.

clues.label: Sport
clues.clue: Nigeria's national football team are the Super ___.

themeHint: Hot, bright and needs oxygen.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Guy ___, whose failed 1605 plot is remembered with bonfires each November.
clues.fact: Bonfire Night on 5 November marks the failed Gunpowder Plot of 1605.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Flying beetle whose tail glows in the dark on summer nights.
clues.fact: Fireflies make light through a chemical reaction called bioluminescence.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Japan's tallest mountain, a snow-capped volcano.
clues.fact: Mount Fuji last erupted in 1707.

clues.clue: Hard stone struck against steel to make sparks.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Cooking style where brandy is poured over a dish and set alight at the table.
clues.fact: Crepes Suzette is a French dessert famously set alight before serving.

clues.label: Job
clues.clue: Brave worker who sprays water on blazes and rescues people.
clues.fact: Ancient Rome had organised firefighting teams called the Vigiles.

themeHint: Think of things that go very, very quickly.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Enzo ___, Italian founder of a famous red racing-car company.
clues.fact: The company's logo shows a black prancing horse.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Bird of prey; its peregrine kind is the fastest animal on Earth when diving.

clues.clue: Nordic country whose quick rally and racing drivers are nicknamed 'Flying' after its people.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Supersonic military aircraft built for air combat.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Burgers and fries served in minutes at a drive-through.
clues.fact: The first McDonald's restaurant opened in California in 1940.

clues.label: Sport
clues.clue: Top motor-racing series with Grand Prix races around the world.
clues.fact: The first Formula One World Championship race was held at Silverstone in 1950.

themeHint: Precious, shiny and yellow.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Fairy-tale girl who tasted the three bears' porridge.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Orange pet fish often kept in a round bowl.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: West African country once called the Gold Coast.
clues.fact: In 1957 Ghana became one of the first sub-Saharan African countries to gain independence.

clues.clue: Shiny brick of precious metal stored in bank vaults.

clues.clue: Sweet amber pancake topping sold in a green tin with a lion on it.

clues.label: Film
clues.clue: 1964 James Bond film whose villain is obsessed with a precious yellow metal.
clues.fact: In Goldfinger, a woman is famously found painted all over in gold.

themeHint: 25 December.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Grumpy green Dr. Seuss character who tried to steal a holiday.
clues.fact: Dr. Seuss published 'How the Grinch Stole Christmas!' in 1957.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Bird roasted for the Cratchit family's festive dinner in A Christmas Carol.
clues.fact: Roast goose was a traditional Christmas dinner in Britain before turkey became popular.

clues.clue: Santa's cave-like den where children visit him in shops.

clues.clue: Wrapped item placed under the tree for someone you love.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Spiced biscuit dough used to build little decorated houses and men.
clues.fact: Gingerbread is flavoured with ginger and often sweetened with molasses or honey.

clues.label: Decoration
clues.clue: Rope of tinsel or greenery hung around the tree or over a doorway.
clues.fact: Evergreen garlands were used in midwinter celebrations long before Christmas trees.

themeHint: Think of the gods on Mount Olympus.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Super-strong hero, son of Zeus, who completed twelve impossible labours.
clues.fact: The Greeks called him Heracles; Hercules is the Roman version of his name.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Pegasus was a winged one of these.
clues.fact: In myth, Pegasus sprang from Medusa's neck when Perseus cut off her head.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Gloomy underworld of the dead, named after the god who ruled it.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Hades owned one that made its wearer invisible; Perseus borrowed it to face Medusa.
clues.fact: Ancient Greek hoplite soldiers often wore a bronze Corinthian-style one that covered most of the face.

clues.clue: Myth says bees fed baby Zeus this sweet golden food in a cave on Crete.
clues.fact: Bees make it from flower nectar, and stored properly it can keep for an extremely long time.

clues.label: Monster
clues.clue: Many-headed serpent: cut off one head and two more grew back.
clues.fact: Hercules killed it as his second labour, with help from his nephew Iolaus.

themeHint: Old MacDonald had one.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Swiss storybook girl who goes to live with her grandfather and his goats in the Alps.

clues.label: Food

clues.label: Season

themeHint: Look up after a shower on a sunny day.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Greek goddess of the rainbow and messenger of the gods.

clues.label: Food

clues.label: Colour

clues.label: Place

clues.label: Thing

clues.label: Food

clues.label: Drink

clues.fact: Sweet tea served cold is a famous tradition in the southern United States.

themeHint: Hot, green and full of vines.

clues.label: Food

clues.label: Film

themeHint: Yo ho ho!

clues.label: Name

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Black flag with a white skull and crossbones.

clues.label: Treasure
clues.clue: Rubies, emeralds and diamonds heaped inside a buried chest.

themeHint: Land of the rising sun.

themeHint: The colour of grass.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Banjo-playing frog who sings that it's not easy being green.

themeHint: The room where meals are made.

themeHint: Where you'd find a shed and flowerbeds.

clues.fact: Millions cluster together on fir trees in the mountains of central Mexico each winter.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Big industrial city in the north, a host of the 1986 and 2026 football World Cups.
clues.fact: It is one of the country's largest cities, ringed by dramatic mountains.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Pair of rattles shaken in time to Latin music, often made from gourds and seeds.
clues.fact: They are usually played in pairs, one in each hand.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Rich, dark sauce often made with chillies and a hint of chocolate.
clues.fact: Both Puebla and Oaxaca claim to be the home of this famous sauce.

clues.label: Music
clues.clue: Strolling band in big sombreros, with trumpets, violins and guitars.
clues.fact: UNESCO added this musical tradition to its list of intangible cultural heritage in 2011.

themeHint: Six legs and creepy-crawly.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Little Miss ___ sat on a tuffet until a spider frightened her away.
clues.fact: The nursery rhyme was first printed in the early 1800s.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Whining biter that can spread malaria.
clues.fact: Only female mosquitoes bite, as they need blood to produce their eggs.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Tall earth tower built by termites on the African savanna.
clues.fact: Termite mounds have air channels that help keep the nest inside cool.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Curved lens on a handle for taking a closer look at tiny bugs.
clues.fact: On a sunny day it can focus sunlight enough to start a fire.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Chunky caterpillar eaten as a protein-rich snack in southern Africa.
clues.fact: It is the caterpillar of the emperor moth and feeds on mopane tree leaves.

clues.label: Insect
clues.clue: Green insect that holds its front legs together as if praying.
clues.fact: It can turn its head almost 180 degrees to look over its shoulder.

themeHint: When the sun goes down and the moon comes up.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Greek goddess who personified the dark hours after sunset.
clues.fact: In Greek myth even Zeus was said to fear angering her.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Small brown bird famous for its beautiful song after dark.
clues.fact: It is mostly unpaired males that sing through the night, to attract a mate.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Spot at the top of the world where winter brings months of darkness.
clues.fact: At the North Pole the sun sets once a year and stays down for about six months.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Small dim lamp left on so children aren't scared of the dark.
clues.fact: Many modern plug-in ones use LEDs and very little electricity.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Warm drink taken just before bed; also an old-fashioned sleeping hat.
clues.fact: Before central heating, people often wore cloth caps in bed to keep their heads warm.

clues.label: Word
clues.clue: Describes owls, bats and other animals that are active after dark.
clues.fact: Many desert animals are active at night to avoid the heat of the day.

themeHint: Grab some popcorn.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Keanu Reeves' hero who takes the red pill in The Matrix.
clues.fact: The Matrix (1999) made 'bullet time' slow-motion effects famous.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Simba's lioness best friend in The Lion King.
clues.fact: Beyonce voiced her in the 2019 remake.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Magical land reached through the back of a wardrobe.
clues.fact: The first Narnia book published was The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe in 1950.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Harry Potter's first racing broomstick, a ___ Two Thousand.
clues.fact: Nimbus is also the name for a dark rain cloud.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Cinema snack of tortilla chips smothered in melted cheese.
clues.fact: They are said to have been invented in Mexico in 1943 by Ignacio 'Nacho' Anaya.

clues.label: Film
clues.clue: Nickname of Nigeria's booming film industry, which makes more films each year than Hollywood.
clues.fact: Nollywood took off in the 1990s with straight-to-video films, and 1992's Living in Bondage is often called its first big hit.

themeHint: Think of the continent the Sahara sits on.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Masked Nigerian striker who fired Napoli to an Italian league title and was named Africa's best player.
clues.fact: Victor Osimhen was named CAF African Footballer of the Year for 2023.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Shy Congo forest animal with zebra-striped legs; its closest relative is the giraffe.
clues.fact: The okapi is found in the wild only in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Capital city of Burkina Faso, famous for its biennial pan-African film festival.
clues.fact: Ouagadougou hosts FESPACO, one of Africa's largest film festivals.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Tall, four-sided stone pillar with a pointed top, first carved by ancient Egyptians.
clues.fact: Ancient Egyptian obelisks now stand in cities such as Rome, Paris, London and New York.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Green pod vegetable that turns soups slimy; loved in West African stews.
clues.fact: Okra is thought to have originated in Africa and is also known as ladies' fingers.

clues.label: Bird
clues.clue: The world's largest bird cannot fly but can outrun most animals on the savanna.
clues.fact: Ostriches lay the largest eggs of any living bird.

themeHint: Think of labs, experiments and microscopes.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Physicist who led the atomic bomb project; Cillian Murphy played him in a 2023 film.
clues.fact: The 2023 film about J. Robert Oppenheimer won the Oscar for Best Picture.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Scientists marvel at this clever eight-armed sea creature with three hearts.
clues.fact: An octopus has blue blood and can change colour in a fraction of a second.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Building with a domed roof and big telescopes for studying the stars.
clues.fact: Chile's dry Atacama Desert hosts some of the world's major telescopes thanks to its clear skies.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Lab screen that draws electrical signals as moving wave shapes.
clues.fact: Early versions of this instrument used cathode-ray tubes like old televisions.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Thin skin from this layered bulb is a classic first sample under school microscopes.
clues.fact: The skin cells of this vegetable are large and easy to see, which is why it is used in school labs.

clues.label: Element
clues.clue: Gas with the symbol O that we need to breathe.
clues.fact: Oxygen is the most abundant element in Earth's crust by mass.

themeHint: Think of the country of the Eiffel Tower.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: French scientist who gave his name to heating milk to kill germs.
clues.fact: Louis Pasteur developed early vaccines against rabies and anthrax.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Curly-coated dog, the national dog of France, often given fancy haircuts.
clues.fact: Despite its French fame, the poodle is believed to have originated in Germany as a water dog.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: City of light on the River Seine, home to the Louvre.
clues.fact: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair in this city.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: French car maker whose badge shows a lion.
clues.fact: Peugeot began as a family business making tools and coffee grinders before cars.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Flaky French breakfast pastry with a dark, sweet bar baked inside.
clues.fact: In south-west France this pastry is often called a chocolatine.

clues.label: Sport
clues.clue: Game of throwing metal balls towards a small wooden jack, played in village squares.
clues.fact: Petanque was invented in the south of France in the early 1900s.

themeHint: Think of the Amazon and the Andes.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Brazilian football legend nicknamed O Rei, the King.
clues.fact: Pele is the only player to have won three FIFA World Cups.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Sharp-toothed fish of Amazon rivers, famous for feeding frenzies.
clues.fact: Many piranha species actually eat plants and seeds as well as meat.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Andean country home to Machu Picchu and Lima.
clues.fact: Lake Titicaca, on Peru's border with Bolivia, is one of the highest navigable lakes in the world.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Woollen blanket with a hole for your head, worn in the Andes.
clues.fact: Ponchos have been worn in the Andes since before the Spanish arrived.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: This staple tuber was first farmed in the Andes before spreading worldwide.
clues.fact: The potato was first domesticated in the Andes of present-day Peru and Bolivia.

clues.label: Region
clues.clue: Windswept land of glaciers and mountains at the southern tip of Argentina and Chile.
clues.fact: Patagonia's Torres del Paine and Perito Moreno Glacier draw visitors from around the world.

themeHint: Think of a colour that means stop.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Reindeer with a glowing nose who guided Santa's sleigh.
clues.fact: Rudolph first appeared in a 1939 booklet given away by a US department store.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Small garden bird with a bright orange-red breast, a symbol of winter cards.
clues.fact: The European robin often follows gardeners to catch worms turned up by digging.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Smallest US state, which gave its name to a famous breed of chicken with rusty feathers.
clues.fact: The Rhode Island Red is the official state bird of Rhode Island.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Precious gemstone, the 40th wedding anniversary stone.
clues.fact: Rubies and sapphires are both forms of the same mineral, corundum.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Soft berry made of tiny bumps; it leaves a hollow when pulled from the plant.
clues.fact: A raspberry is made up of many small drupelets, each with its own seed.

clues.label: Flower
clues.clue: Thorny flower given in bunches on Valentine's Day.
clues.fact: The rose is the national flower of England and the United States.

themeHint: Think of animals that live in your home.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Old-fashioned name for a pet dog, also a word for a wanderer.
clues.fact: NASA's Mars vehicles are also called by this word, which means a wanderer.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Long-eared pet that lives in a hutch and nibbles carrots.
clues.fact: A rabbit's front teeth never stop growing.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Shelter where abandoned cats and dogs wait to be adopted (two words).
clues.fact: Battersea in London, founded in 1860, is one of the oldest animal shelters in the world.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Ribbon prize pinned on the winner at a pet show.
clues.fact: In the UK a red one usually means first place, while in the US first place is usually blue.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Dried grapes that are poisonous to dogs, so never share them.
clues.fact: Grapes and their dried form can cause kidney failure in dogs.

clues.label: Breed
clues.clue: Powerful black-and-tan German guard dog breed.
clues.fact: The breed is named after the German town of Rottweil.

themeHint: Think of capes, masks and saving the day.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Caped hero from Krypton who works as reporter Clark Kent.
clues.fact: This hero first appeared in Action Comics in 1938.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: A bite from one of these gave Peter Parker his powers.
clues.fact: Weight for weight, the silk of this creature can be stronger than steel.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Kansas farming town where young Clark Kent grew up.
clues.fact: A TV series named after this town ran for ten seasons from 2001.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Captain America's round, star-marked piece of defensive kit.
clues.fact: Captain America first appeared in comics in 1941.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Popeye gulps this leafy green from a can to get super strength.
clues.fact: Spinach is rich in iron, but the iron is not easily absorbed by the body.

clues.label: Role
clues.clue: Helper hero who fights alongside the main one, like Robin with Batman.
clues.fact: Robin first appeared alongside Batman in 1940.

themeHint: Think of kilts and bagpipes.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Edinburgh-born actor who was the first James Bond on film (full name).
clues.fact: Sean Connery won an Oscar for his role in The Untouchables.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Small, sturdy horse from the islands far north of the Scottish mainland.
clues.fact: Shetland ponies are among the strongest horses for their size.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Seaside town on the Fife coast known as the home of golf.
clues.fact: The University of St Andrews, founded in the 1400s, is Scotland's oldest university.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Pouch worn on a belt at the front of a kilt.
clues.fact: Kilts traditionally have no pockets, which is why a sporran is worn.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Crumbly, buttery biscuit, often sold in tartan tins.
clues.fact: Classic shortbread uses just three ingredients: butter, sugar and flour.

clues.label: Fish
clues.clue: Pink-fleshed fish that leaps up Scottish rivers to spawn.
clues.fact: Salmon return to the river where they hatched in order to breed.

themeHint: Think of 31 October.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Director of Edward Scissorhands and The Nightmare Before Christmas (full name).
clues.fact: Tim Burton worked as an animator at Disney early in his career.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Big, hairy spider that makes a classic creepy costume prop.
clues.fact: Some female tarantulas can live for more than 20 years.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Region of Romania where Bram Stoker set Count Dracula's castle.
clues.fact: Bran Castle in this region is often marketed as Dracula's Castle.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Engraved stone marking a grave, a favourite spooky decoration.
clues.fact: Tombstone is also the name of a famous Wild West town in Arizona.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Fruit on a stick coated in hard caramel, a treat at autumn fairs.
clues.fact: In the US a similar treat is called a candy apple.

clues.label: Tradition
clues.clue: Children in costume knock on doors saying this three-word phrase.
clues.fact: Trick-or-treating became widespread in North America in the mid-1900s.

themeHint: Think small. Very small.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Peter Pan's little fairy who sprinkles pixie dust.
clues.fact: Tinker Bell first appeared in J. M. Barrie's 1904 play Peter Pan.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Tiny eight-legged bloodsucker that clings to dogs and deer.
clues.fact: Ticks are arachnids, related to spiders rather than insects.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Pacific island nation, one of the smallest countries on Earth, with the web suffix .tv.
clues.fact: Tuvalu earns income by licensing its .tv internet domain.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Little metal cap that protects your fingertip when sewing.
clues.fact: Thimbles have been used for sewing since at least Roman times.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Spanish small plates, shared with friends in bars.
clues.fact: Tapas comes from the Spanish verb tapar, meaning to cover.

clues.label: Measure
clues.clue: Smallest common kitchen spoon, used for sugar in tea.
clues.fact: In recipes, three of these spoons make one tablespoon.

themeHint: Think of a boot-shaped country.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Venetian composer of The Four Seasons.
clues.fact: Antonio Vivaldi was nicknamed the Red Priest because of his red hair.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Venomous snake family; every dangerous snake in Italy belongs to it.
clues.fact: Vipers have long hinged fangs that fold back when the mouth is closed.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Italian city of canals, gondolas and St Mark's Square.
clues.fact: Venice is built on more than 100 small islands in a lagoon.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Classic Italian scooter whose name means wasp.
clues.fact: The Vespa was first launched by the Piaggio company in 1946.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Modena's famous balsamic kind of this sour liquid is aged in wooden barrels.
clues.fact: Traditional balsamic from Modena must be aged for at least 12 years.

clues.label: Volcano
clues.clue: Volcano that buried Pompeii in AD 79, still towering over Naples.
clues.fact: The eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79 also buried the nearby town of Herculaneum.

themeHint: Think of hearts and 14 February.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Saint whose feast day on 14 February is for sweethearts.
clues.fact: Saint Valentine's Day became linked with romance in the Middle Ages.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Prairie species of this small rodent are famous for pairing up for life.
clues.fact: Prairie voles are among the few mammals that form lifelong pair bonds.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Northern Italian city where Romeo and Juliet is set.
clues.fact: Tourists in this city visit a balcony said to be Juliet's.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Sheer fabric covering a bride's face.
clues.fact: Wedding veils date back to ancient Rome.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Sweet flavour from orchid pods, used in wedding cakes and ice cream.
clues.fact: Vanilla comes from the pods of an orchid native to Mexico.

clues.label: Flower
clues.clue: Roses are red, these are blue, sugar is sweet, and so are you.
clues.fact: Violets are edible and are sometimes candied to decorate cakes.

themeHint: Think of once upon a time.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Girl who flies to Neverland with Peter Pan.
clues.fact: The name Wendy became popular after Peter Pan was first staged in 1904.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Big bad creature who blew down houses and tricked Red Riding Hood.
clues.fact: Wolves live and hunt in family groups called packs.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Alice fell down a rabbit hole into this strange land.
clues.fact: Lewis Carroll wrote Alice's Adventures in Wonderland for a real girl named Alice Liddell.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Stick a fairy godmother waves to work her magic.
clues.fact: Cinderella's fairy godmother turns a pumpkin into a coach.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Thumbelina slept in a shell of this nut, polished as a cradle.
clues.fact: In Andersen's tale, Thumbelina's cradle is a polished walnut shell.

clues.label: Character
clues.clue: Hansel and Gretel's captor lived in a gingerbread house and rode a broomstick in other tales.
clues.fact: Hansel and Gretel was collected by the Brothers Grimm and first published in 1812.

themeHint: Think of songs, singers and dancing.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Lagos-born Afrobeats star who sang on Drake's chart-topping One Dance.
clues.fact: Wizkid won a Grammy in 2021 for Brown Skin Girl, his song with Beyoncé, Blue Ivy and Saint Jhn.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Humpback types of this ocean giant sing long, haunting songs.
clues.fact: Male humpbacks sing complex songs that change gradually over the years.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: New York farm festival of 1969 where Jimi Hendrix played.
clues.fact: The festival was held in Bethel, New York, some distance from the town it was named after.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Small instrument a referee blows to stop play.
clues.fact: A tin version of this instrument is common in Irish folk music.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Fruit in the title of a Grammy-winning Harry Styles hit with sugar.
clues.fact: Watermelon Sugar won Harry Styles a Grammy for Best Pop Solo Performance.

clues.label: Dance
clues.clue: Elegant ballroom dance in three-four time, loved in Vienna.
clues.fact: Johann Strauss II wrote The Blue Danube, a famous piece in this dance style.
